intro: Ten fresh adventures for Minecraft Bedrock, counting down to the coolest. Each one works in game version 26.50 (Wilderness Bound). None of them were in Volume 1.

items.title: Plant a Firefly Garden
items.why: Firefly bushes fill the dark with tiny glowing bugs. Plant your own garden, and your base will twinkle every evening.
items.where: On grass near water in most of the Overworld, and anywhere in swamps. Wandering traders sometimes sell them too.
steps: Find a firefly bush near water or in a swamp. Look for tiny glowing dots on its leaves.
Break it with your hand. It always drops itself.
Plant it on grass, dirt or moss next to your home.
Use bone meal on the bush. It spreads to the blocks around it.
Keep lanterns at least 2 blocks away. Fireflies only come out where it is dim.
Wait for dusk, then watch the fireflies drift up into the air.
need: Emeralds (if you buy a bush from a wandering trader)
items.wow: At night, firefly bushes give off a soft buzz. They only buzz if nothing solid sits on top of them.
items.note: In Bedrock, fireflies can appear up to 10 blocks away from their bush. Leave open space around your garden.
items.scene_idea: A small pond at night with Coarse Dirt, Moss Block and Podzol banks, a row of Firefly Bushes, Sugar Cane and an oak tree, plus one Lantern on an Oak Fence post well away from the bushes.

items.title: Take a Golden-Hour Photo Tour
items.why: Vibrant Visuals gives Minecraft real shadows, shining water and sunlight that glows through leaves. When the sun is low, shadows stretch long across your builds.
items.where: Anywhere in the Overworld, at dawn or sunset. The sun rises in the east and sets in the west.
steps: Check your device. On iPad, Vibrant Visuals needs an A12 or M1 chip or newer.
Open Settings, then Video. Set Graphics Mode to Vibrant Visuals.
Sleep in a bed. You wake at dawn, with the sun low in the east.
Visit water, leaves and copper. Water reflects the sky, sunlight glows through leaves, and copper shines.
Come back at sunset and face west, when the sunlight turns orange. Snap a screenshot of your favorite build.
need: A device that runs Vibrant Visuals
items.wow: In Minecraft, the sun moves more slowly at sunrise and sunset. That gives you extra time for photos.
items.note: Playing split-screen with a friend? The game switches back to Fancy or Simple graphics.
items.scene_idea: A small Cherry Planks cottage at sunset with a Cut Copper roof, Glass Pane windows and Cherry Trapdoor shutters, beside a 3 x 3 pool with a Smooth Stone rim and a cherry tree.

items.title: Build a Music Disc Trophy Wall
items.why: Music discs are hidden all over the world. Hunt them down and show them off on shelves, like trophies.
items.where: On a wall in your base. The discs come from ruins, caves and one very silly mob.
steps: Strip 6 logs of the same wood with an axe. They craft into 6 shelves.
Put the shelves in a row on a wall. Each shelf holds 3 discs.
Brush suspicious gravel in buried trail ruins. One of the prizes is the Relic disc.
Search minecart chests in mineshafts inside sulfur caves. That is where the Bounce disc hides.
Lava Chicken comes from a chicken jockey, a baby zombie riding a chicken. Win against the tiny rider while it is still on the chicken. The chicken can go free.
Hold a disc and use a shelf slot to put it on show. Add a jukebox to play your favorite.
items.wow: About 46 seconds into Lava Chicken, villager sounds start playing the tune.
items.note: There are 22 music discs. Eight shelves can hold all of them, with 2 spots to spare.
items.scene_idea: A slice of a cozy room: a Birch Planks wall between Stripped Spruce Log pillars, six Spruce Shelves in a row, two Copper Lanterns, and a red rug with two cushions on a Spruce Slab floor.

items.title: Start a Copper Trumpet Band
items.why: Put copper under a note block and it plays a trumpet. As the copper turns green, the horn changes its sound.
items.where: Anywhere you like. Build a stage at your base or in a village square.
steps: Craft note blocks: 8 planks around 1 redstone dust.
Put a Block of Copper under each note block. Keep the space above the note block empty.
Use a note block to raise it by one note. Each one has 25 notes, two full octaves.
Mix copper ages. Exposed copper sounds different, and weathered and oxidized copper play an octave lower.
Use honeycomb on each copper block to wax it. Now its sound will never change.
Put a button on the side of each note block, then play a tune!
need: Block of Copper (one for each note block)
items.wow: Note blocks can be heard up to 48 blocks away. Your whole village will hear the band.
items.note: Copper too green? Scrape it with an axe. The first scrape takes off any wax. Each scrape after that removes one stage of green.
items.scene_idea: A Polished Andesite stage with four Note Blocks in a row, standing on Waxed Block of Copper, Waxed Exposed Copper, Waxed Weathered Copper and Waxed Oxidized Copper, with a Stone Button on the front of each.

items.title: Watch the Pale Garden Wake Up
items.why: When night falls, the eyeblossoms in the pale garden open their glowing eyes. It is quiet, spooky and very pretty.
items.where: Pale gardens are rare gray forests next to dark forests, high on hills and mountain slopes. A Pale Garden Camp Map from an abandoned camp leads to one.
steps: Before sunset, build a little hut with glass windows at the edge of the garden.
When night falls, watch the eyeblossoms open. Each one tells its neighbors, so they open in a wave.
Pick a few open eyeblossoms to take home. Use bone meal on one, and more grow on the grass around it.
For resin, tap a creaking once at night. It can't be hurt, but resin clumps grow on logs near its heart.
Collect the resin clumps. Smelt them in a furnace to make resin bricks.
Put 4 resin bricks together to craft a block of orange Resin Bricks.
items.wow: Music fades away when you walk into a pale garden. It comes back when you leave.
items.note: A creaking only moves when you look away from it. Walk back into your hut while facing it.
items.scene_idea: A corner of pale garden at night: Pale Moss Block ground, two pale oak trees hung with Pale Hanging Moss, a patch of Open Eyeblossoms, and a tiny Glass hut with a Pale Oak roof and a Resin Brick Slab step.

items.title: Camp Out Under the Stars
items.why: Wilderness Bound added cushions to sit on and straw beds to sleep on. Now you can camp out all over the Overworld.
items.where: Anywhere in the Overworld. Abandoned camps also have straw beds and cushions you can borrow.
steps: Turn 3 wool into 6 wool slabs. Then 3 matching wool slabs make 1 cushion.
Craft straw beds: 3 hay bales make 4 straw beds.
Craft a campfire from 3 sticks, 1 coal or charcoal, and 3 logs.
Place cushions around the fire. They sit on the ground, on slabs or on stairs. Use one to sit down.
At night, sleep on a straw bed. In the morning it is gone, and your spawn point stays at home.
items.wow: From September 26 to October 2, 2026, Bedrock players placed 200 million cushions. They placed 50 million straw beds too. It was a community challenge, and they did it!
items.note: A straw bed breaks after one night and does not set your spawn point. Keep a real bed at home.
items.scene_idea: A Campfire at night on Coarse Dirt and Dirt Path, ringed by four colored Cushions on Oak Slabs, with two Straw Beds under a White Wool Stairs tent and a pile of firewood logs.

items.title: Follow the Camp Map Trail
items.why: Abandoned camps hide chests that can hold maps. Each camp map leads to another camp, so one find can start a long adventure.
items.where: On the surface in 18 kinds of biomes, like forests, taigas, meadows, swamps and cherry groves.
steps: Explore forests, taigas, meadows and swamps. Look for a white tent made of wool stairs.
Open the chests and barrels. Camp chests can hold a camp map.
Hold the map and walk toward the camp marker. It always leads to a camp in a different biome.
Look closely around the tent. Some camps hide an old green copper chest under blocks, with better loot.
Keep going! Camp chests can also hold maps to mineshafts, desert pyramids, warm ocean ruins and ancient cities.
items.wow: Abandoned camps can be put together in 8,820 different ways.
items.note: Turn on Show Coordinates in your world settings. Write down where each camp is.
items.scene_idea: An abandoned camp corner: a White Wool Stairs tent on Spruce Fence poles, Barrels, a Chest and a Cartography Table, a Dirt Path trail, and an Oxidized Copper Chest half dug out of Coarse Dirt and Gravel.

items.title: Keep a Baby Animal Tiny Forever
items.why: A golden dandelion stops a baby animal from growing up. Your calf or lamb can stay little for as long as you like.
items.where: Any farm or pen where you keep animals.
steps: Feed wheat to two cows. A baby appears, and you unlock the golden dandelion recipe.
Turn a gold ingot into 9 gold nuggets.
Place 8 gold nuggets around 1 dandelion to craft a golden dandelion.
Use it on the baby. Green sparkles pop out, and it stops growing.
Changed your mind? Give it a second golden dandelion, and it starts growing again.
items.wow: Most baby animals grow up in 20 minutes. Snifflets, the baby sniffers, take 40 minutes.
items.note: Golden dandelions do not work on baby villagers or baby zombie horses.
items.scene_idea: A small Oak Fence pen with an Oak Fence Gate, a Cauldron and a Hay Bale under a little shelter, an empty spot for the baby animal, and two planters of Golden Dandelions by the path.

items.title: Tame a Zombie Horse
items.why: Zombie horses gallop out at night with a zombie rider. Unseat the rider like a jousting knight, and the horse can be yours.
items.where: Plains, savannas and snowy plains, at night. A zombie with an iron spear rides each one.
steps: Before dark, craft a saddle (3 leather, 1 iron ingot) and leather horse armor (7 leather).
At night, look across plains and savannas for a zombie riding a horse. They don't appear on Peaceful.
Unseat the rider, like a knight at a joust. Then beat the zombie before it climbs back on.
On its own, the zombie horse is calm. Climb on again and again until it stops bucking you off.
Hearts mean it is tamed! Put the saddle on so you can steer.
Add the horse armor. It keeps your zombie horse safe in sunlight.
need: Your own armor and a shield
items.wow: Red mushrooms heal a tamed zombie horse. Hold one up and it will follow you.
items.note: Zombie horses can't be bred, so every one you tame is special.
items.scene_idea: A small jousting yard: a Dirt Path lane split by an Oak Fence rail, Red and White Wool posts at each end, and a Spruce Planks stable with two stalls, one left empty for the horse.

items.title: Ride a Nautilus Underwater
items.why: A tamed nautilus is an underwater horse. While you ride, your air stops running out. Explore the seafloor for ages!
items.where: In every kind of ocean, a little below the waves, between Y 38 and Y 58.
steps: Craft a saddle from 3 leather and 1 iron ingot.
Catch pufferfish with a fishing rod. Or scoop one into a water bucket in a warm ocean.
Swim down to find a grown-up nautilus. Hold a fish and it swims over to you.
Feed it pufferfish. Each one has a 1 in 3 chance to tame it.
Once it is tamed, put the saddle on and climb aboard.
Hold jump to charge a dash. It zooms you up to about 12 blocks forward.
items.wow: Dash up near the surface, and you both leap out of the water. The jump is about 6 blocks!
items.note: Don't hit a wild nautilus, or it dashes back at you. Riding only pauses your air, so check your bubbles before you hop off.
items.scene_idea: A seafloor patch of Sand and Gravel under clear water, with Kelp along the back, a coral reef in five colors with Sea Pickles, and a small Prismarine Bricks arch with Sea Lanterns. The open water in the middle is where the nautilus swims.
